text:
Sam K: Heads up — noticed a ~12% p99 latency tail increase on host ingress after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Quick triage shows most of the extra CPU is host-side (tokenization + small gRPC writes).

Anya V: ugh. is this across all models or just certain seq lengths?

Sam K: Mostly short requests (<200 tokens) and streaming paths. Flamegraph from the host preparse worker attached inline. Key hotspots: writev syscalls, utf8-normalize, and a parse-state machine allocation.

Sam K: ```
# perf script sampling (summary)
writev  42.3%  (syscall)
utf8_normalize 18.4%  (host/tokenizer.cc:212)
parse_state::advance 12.1%  (host/parse.cc:87)
kvcache::lookup  6.0%  (runtime/kvcache.cc)
other 21.2%
```

Mike L: can you paste the exact request sizes? this smells like tiny-chunk gRPC overhead + no coalescing on the host proxy.

Sam K: here — when we split streaming fragments at 64-128b we do lots of small writev calls. avg payload around 120B, median 95B. kvcache hit-rate dropped from 86% -> 67% during canary (shard rebalance coincident).

Tanya R: drops in kv hit-rate amplifies kernel selection churn since warmup paths prefer different kernels. did kernel-selector increase model switching?

Sam K: yes — new scoring added sequence-length-weighted kernel preference; for very short sequences it picked the slim-kernel which has slightly different cache-access pattern. Combined with kv miss storms it elevated host CPU.

Anya V: actionable? rollback kernel change for streaming routes and throttle tiny writes?

Mike L: +1. short-term: pin kernel selector to old policy for routes with streaming:true or avg_payload < 256. mid-term: add write coalescing in host proxy (buffer up to 1ms or 512b) and increase preparse batching threshold for short sessions.

Sam K: testing patch locally: host-proxy coalesce=1ms reduces writev count by ~6x in my run, p99 drops ~9%. command I used:

Sam K: ```bash
# reproduce load
wrk -t4 -c200 -d30s --script=stream_small.lua http://localhost:8080
# capture strace on worker
strace -f -tt -e trace=writev -p $(pidof host-proxy) 2>&1 | head -n 40
```

infra-bot: deploy job 4672 started for host-proxy/coalesce-1ms (canary to 5% hosts). https://ci.example/4672

Tanya R: kvcache prewarm idea: on rollout trigger a lightweight async fanout to repopulate hot keys (based on recent top-100 keys) so new kernel choice doesn't hit cold misses. cheap and probably effective.

Sam K: good idea. I'll add a prewarm hook tied to shard reassign. Also I'll open a small PR to pin kernel selector for streaming routes + a canary config toggle.

Anya V: please also add a perf test to release pipeline that runs short-seq streaming profile (script above) so we don't regress again.

Mike L: I'll add telemetry counters for writev counts and avg-fragment-size per route. quick dashboard should show before/after.

Sam K: action items:
- Sam: PR to pin kernel selector for streaming routes (canary flag)
- Sam: prewarm hook for kvcache on shard reassignment
- Mike: telemetry + dashboard for writev / frag-size
- Anya: add short-seq streaming profile to CI release checks
- Ops: monitor job 4672 canary, roll back if p99 increases >5%

Sam K: thanks all :thumbsup:

Mike L: :rocket:

Tanya R: :eyes:

Anya V: noted, will follow up on CI item tomorrow.
